title: Every Sky Primitive instance is tracked through an identically shaped Hub Document with status-partitioned directories
content:
Launch Agent 7 repeats one structure verbatim for every primitive it uses. A Primitive Hub Document (A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.1, A.6.1.1.8.2.1.2.1, A.6.1.1.8.2.1.3.1, A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.1) "organize[s] all base information relevant to Launch Agent 7's usage" of that primitive, and always contains: a Global Activation Status, an Active Instances Directory, a Completed Instances Directory, an In Progress Invocations Directory, and a Hub Data Repository.

The Hub Data Repository in turn always contains an Archived Invocations/Instances subtree split into Failed Invocations and Suspended Instances (e.g. A.6.1.1.8.2.1.1.1.5.1.1 and .5.1.2).

The uniformity is the point. Because the shape is fixed, a reader or tool can locate any primitive's live state, history, and failures without knowing anything about what that primitive does — the Artifact is navigable by structure rather than by prose. It also means an empty directory is meaningful: absence of an Active Instance is a positive statement about the Agent's state, not missing documentation.

The cost is high boilerplate volume: most of the Artifact's units are structural scaffolding carrying no claim, which is the trade the design accepts in exchange for machine-legible uniformity.
description: Each primitive gets a Hub Document exposing Active, Completed and In Progress Invocation directories plus a Hub Data Repository archiving failed Invocations and suspended Instances.
